thread:
incident-bot: 🔔 INCIDENT: Dedicated pool eu-dedicated-1 p99 latency > 6s for streaming/generate (2m window). Auto-paging oncall.

maria: @alen you up? seeing streaming stalls, p95 ~1.6s -> 2.1s, p99 ~6.2s on live traffic. Affected customers: 3 large tenants.

alen: on it — grabbing telemetry. quick question: is this new deploy or capacity? I see spike at 17:46 UTC.

janelle: nothing in deploy channel flagged. last platform deploy was 3h ago.

maria: grafana: queue depth for eu-dedicated-1 went from 20 -> 420 over 90s. Warmup success rate fell to 30%. KV-cache misses up 5x.

ops-bot: metric snapshot: 
- request_rate: +300%
- queue_depth: 420
- warmup_latency_avg: 2.3s
- warmup_failures: 70%

alen: sounds like saturation + warmup handshake delay. Autoscaler didn't add slots fast enough. Checking autoscale logs.

sre-rotation: I see repeated handshake timeouts in pool-autoscaler: 
```
2026-03-15T17:46:10Z autoscaler WARN handshake timeout for slot-request id=xx-9f
2026-03-15T17:46:12Z autoscaler INFO retry slot-request id=xx-9f backoff=2s
2026-03-15T17:46:15Z pool-manager ERROR reserved-slot allocation failed: image-pull slow
```

leo-research: image-pull slow? that would explain warmup. Are we hitting node-level resource pressure (disk/io)?

alen: node metrics show burst of image pulls around 17:45; several nodes hitting docker pull QPS limits from provider. Also kube scheduler pending pods increasing.

maria: immediate mitigation options?

janelle: runbook options: (1) add hot spare nodes to pool (manual), (2) failover traffic to fallback-model (smaller instance) for affected customers, (3) pause streaming for heavy sessions.

alen: I'll try manual pool carve-out first: provisioning ephemeral nodes to bypass the autoscaler backlog.

ops-bot: running command suggested by runbook: 
```
# allocate 4 hotshot nodes and attach to eu-dedicated-1
providerctl nodes create --region eu --type hotshot-2g --count 4 --tag dedicated-hotshot
redwoodctl pool attach-nodes --pool eu-dedicated-1 --nodes tag:dedicated-hotshot
```

maria: doing customer comms: pinging cs for affected tenants. @sam-cs can you notify customers and request reduced traffic if possible? mention degraded streaming and possible failover. :loudsound:

sam-cs: pinged primary contacts. one tenant (AcmeCorp) reports realtime stalls impacting demo sessions. they're escalating to their Eng lead. I suggested retry logic and asked them to temporarily reduce concurrent streams.

alen: manual node create in progress. kube pending queue draining a bit. attaching nodes now.

incident-bot: UPDATE: pool nodes attached. warmup success rate climbed from 30% -> 62% in 45s. queue depth down to 120. p99 dropped to 3.4s but still above SLO.

maria: good. still seeing streaming stalls for some sessions — likely long-tail requests that started during cold-warm transition. we should evict stuck sessions gracefully.

janelle: ops option: kill connections older than 60s for streaming endpoints in pool eu-dedicated-1 (graceful close) to unblock backlog. need approval.

alen: agree. queue has a lot of pinned requests holding KV cache locks. killing long-lived stalls should free capacity. I'm going to run eviction with 30s drain.

ops-bot: running: 
```
redwoodctl pool evict-sessions --pool eu-dedicated-1 --min-age 60s --grace 30s
```

leo-research: note — evict will cause some in-flight responses to be truncated; customers will see failed streams. document it in comms.

maria: doing update to customers now: "We are proactively restarting stuck streams to restore capacity; some streams may fail briefly — working on mitigation."

incident-bot: EVENT: evict command completed. freed 85 sessions. queue depth down to 38. p95 back to 1.1s, p99 1.9s.

sam-cs: AcmeCorp confirms sessions restored for their demo users. they saw a few truncated streams but recovered quickly.

alen: follow-ups: autoscaler logs show backlog because provider image registry returned 503s for a short window; autoscaler retried and hit exponential backoff. Need to add local node image cache and increase parallel pull quota.

janelle: file action items: 
- add node-level image cache to k8s node bootstrap (ticket PLATFORM-4578).
- adjust autoscaler retry policy for critical pools (PLATFORM-4579).
- add early-warning alert for image-pull error rate (ALERT-POOL-IMAGE-ERROR).

maria: also add a playbook step to fallback-model routing: if pool warmup success rate < 40% for >60s, route new requests to fallback-medium model to preserve latency SLOs. (ticket PLATFORM-4580).

ops-bot: creating post-incident runbook items and linking logs.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: p99 back under SLO threshold (1.9s) for 5m sliding window. Status: mitigated -> monitoring.

maria: root cause summary for postmortem: provider registry transient 503s led to slow image pulls -> autoscaler backlog + node provisioning delays -> dedicated pool saturation -> queue amplification + KV-cache coldpath -> streaming stalls and p99 SLO breach. Manual provisioning + session eviction restored capacity.

alen: immediate mitigations we used: manual hotshot nodes, session eviction, failover to fallback model (not required), customer comms.

janelle: severity: Sev3 (customer impact on demos, degraded latency). Follow-up: schedule RCA with infra provider and ship PLATFORM-4578/4579/4580.

maria: thanks all for quick work. I'll convert thread into incident report and start the postmortem doc. tagging @sre-rotation for follow-up. :thumbsup:

sre-rotation: noted. i'll own RCA with provider.

incident-bot: LOGS & ARTIFACTS: https://logs.redwood.example/incident/1765436789 | runbook snapshot: https://confluence.redwood.example/incidents/1765436789

maria: closing thread, moving to postmortem board.

alen: one last note — consider adding a soft-cap on concurrent streaming sessions per-customer to reduce blast radius for future bursts. (suggestion)

sam-cs: copying customer feedback into ticket. customers appreciated the quick updates.

incident-bot: thread archived (state: resolved).
